reason: Overconfidence is strongest in interval judgements (stated 80% ranges hold far less often), so range training is the higher-value debias; F-D gets binary calibration first and ranges on evidence. Every finalist uses proper scoring, so honest forecasting maximises points. The live risk is outcome bias: a salient 'This run: +255' teaches luck. F-E's test is underpowered by design and its expected result is signed as 'stop', so it measures nothing that changes the decision.
demand: In every reveal and summary the Expected and Best expected lines come before the This run and Luck lines in DOM order, at equal or larger font size; checked by a Playwright DOM-order and computed-style test.

F-A's finish cue, which removes the luck line, is good design. F-C's weekly schedule and F-D's calendar unlock are return hooks I object to.

reason: "Will this line go up, and how sure are you?" is something anyone gets in five seconds, so F-A or F-E. Words like 'Best expected', 'shortfall' and 'Luck moved this run by +343' will confuse most people. People open this app to see real traders' records; a side game on fake charts is a nice-to-have. So build the cheap version, give it a date, and find out whether anyone plays it twice.
